speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for providing the skin photos; please describe the specific morphology of the rash (e.g., vesicles, pustules, macules) and whether it is pruritic or painful. Additionally, has there been any known exposure to chickenpox or contact with an individual with a rash, and did your mother have a similar rash during your pregnancy?

REQUEST TEST: Tzanck smear and VZV PCR.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The CBC and Tzanck smear results are normal, which makes a classic bacterial infection or typical chickenpox less likely. Can you tell me if the lesions are blanching when pressed, and whether there are any "dewdrop" vesicles on a red base or honey-colored crusts present? Also, has your mother received the Varicella (chickenpox) vaccine, and are there any blisters on your lips or inside your mouth?

REQUEST TEST: Gram stain of skin lesion.
REQUEST TEST: Maternal Varicella IgG titer.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum. The normal CBC, cultures, and viral smears rule out infection and chickenpox; the non-blanching nature of the rash you described is inconsistent with Erythema Toxicum, which typically presents with blanching macules and "dewdrop" vesicles. Please confirm if the lesions have a central white or yellow spot with a surrounding red halo, as this would support my diagnosis.
